studies.label: Field experiment: ChatGPT access in a Chinese technology consulting firm
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Randomization was individual, not by supervisor or department. Table 2 reports independent-samples t tests. The multilevel analyses use employee scores nested within supervisors within departments (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Results); these organizational levels are not randomized clusters. The main table prints intercept variance components for the upper levels, but does not name a robust or cluster-sandwich SE estimator (PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Participants and Procedure, final sample before random assignment; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Results, and PDF p. 7 (printed p. 6), Table 1 note, confirm analyzed total
counts_source.quote: Due to business travel and illnesses, 36 employees did not participate, resulting in a ﬁnal sample of 250 employees.

arms.name: LLM assistance
arms.description: Employees individually received personal ChatGPT accounts through the firm’s API-based interface with usage examples; instructed not to share or discuss the accounts. All treated employees reported use and the usage logs confirmed use (PDF pp. 5-6, printed pp. 4-5).

arms.name: Control (no LLM assistance)
arms.description: Employees received no LLM assistance; no control employee reported ChatGPT use (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

studies.task: At the intervention endpoint, employees wrote suggestions for protecting employee privacy when companies use digital devices; external raters scored these written responses.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT through the firm’s OpenAI API-based interface; underlying model version not stated
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), introduction: In November 2022, OpenAI launched ChatGPT; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Empirical Setting, and PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5), Participants and Procedure, identify the interface and ChatGPT accounts. Year is the named product’s launch year, not an inferred model-version year.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 4), Transparency and Openness: This study is not preregistered.

estimates.outcome: Novelty of privacy-protection response (unadjusted arm comparison)
estimates.measure_detail: Two external raters independently scored each employee’s written privacy-protection response using the consensual assessment technique, from 1 = least to 5 = most. estimates.notes: AI availability while this second-survey response was composed is not stated. The reconciled screening form explicitly leaves this unresolved; question and outcome_with_ai remain null rather than guessing with_ai or after_ai. This is an intervention-endpoint output, with no documented AI-removal test or later retention session. The paper establishes human assessment but does not establish the external raters’ qualifications; measure remains null. Each employee supplied one response, and the reported analyses use employee-level scores rather than treating the raters as independent observations. Arm-specific counts are not printed and are not inferred from the rounded condition mean. Table 2 gives independent-samples t-test p values, arm means and SDs, and Cohen’s d. The t statistic, degrees of freedom, confidence intervals, and the denominator used for d are not printed. The SDs describe employee-level outcome scores, not separate rater scores. Figure 2 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8) plots arm means and standard-error bars without numerical SE labels; no values were read off the figure. The separately recorded condition correlation is another summary of this same outcome and contrast.

not_extracted.what: ChatGPT use, self-reported use frequency, and account-usage logs
not_extracted.reason: Manipulation and compliance checks, not creativity or diversity of employee output (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Experimental Conditions and Manipulation Checks).

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Novelty, covariate-adjusted LLM effects in Table 3 Models 3, 6, and 10
not_extracted.reason: All include attitudinal and motivational controls measured in the second, posttreatment survey. The Controls section identifies these as potential alternative mediators; later models additionally control cognitive job resources and include moderation. Excluded under the rule barring any posttreatment adjustment, including the main novelty model without the named cognitive-resource mediator (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure, Controls, Results and footnote 2; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3).

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: Usefulness, covariate-adjusted LLM effects in Table 3 Models 4, 7, and 11
not_extracted.reason: All include attitudinal and motivational controls measured after treatment; later models additionally control cognitive job resources and include moderation. Excluded under the posttreatment-adjustment rule (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Participants and Procedure, Controls, Results and footnote 2; PDF p. 10, printed p. 9, Table 3). The no-controls multilevel usefulness effect printed in Results is extracted separately.

not_extracted.reason: Main-text footnote 2 says no-controls multilevel models support all creativity measures but gives only a range of p values across outcomes. The exact novelty coefficient, SE, and outcome-specific p value are not printed in the supplied article and cannot be assigned or reconstructed (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, footnote 2). The supplement-manifest entry lists no supplement files.

not_extracted.what: Pooled-sample descriptive means/SDs and correlations among creativity measures, mediators, and moderators
not_extracted.reason: These describe the combined sample or associations between measured variables, not additional randomized-arm contrasts. They are not arm-specific means/SDs. The correlations with randomized LLM condition itself are extracted separately (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Table 1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Dependent Variable: Creativity).

open_items: AI availability during the privacy-protection writing task is unreported. Preserve question = null and outcome_with_ai = null pending task instructions or access records; the screening form also explicitly leaves both unresolved. The question enum in the extraction template has no unknown category, so these intentional nulls require reconciliation rather than an invented classification.
Arm-specific randomized and analyzed participant counts are not printed. Do not infer an equal split from the rounded binary-condition mean or from degrees of freedom.

External-rater qualifications are not stated, so the human_raters versus expert_raters subtype cannot be confirmed. Human assessment of output is established; measure remains null as in the reconciled screening form.

The separate supplement linked on PDF p. 2 is not on file; supplement-manifest.json records no files and a failed access attempt. It is needed for the no-controls novelty multilevel statistics and to resolve the Results reference to Supplemental Table S5 Model 4 versus footnote 2’s reference to Supplemental Materials S4 and its aggregate p-value range.

Table 2 does not define the standardizer for its reported Cohen’s d or print t statistics, degrees of freedom, confidence intervals, or numerical arm SEs. Figure 2’s standard-error bars have no numerical labels and were not digitized.
The underlying ChatGPT model version and its release year are not stated. The study-level tool year records the named ChatGPT product’s documented launch year only.
notes: Extraction B, 2026-10-11. Read the extraction specification and codebook, the reconciled screening and citation records, the local supplement manifest, and the full markdown conversion including all references and editorial history. Reviewed PDF tables and figures first and checked every recorded statistic against PyMuPDF page text. The PDF has no appended supplement or appendix. Statistical inventory for the output outcomes: Table 1 gives full-sample descriptions and correlations with condition; Table 2 gives arm means/SDs, t-test p values and Cohen’s d; Figure 2 repeats arm means with unlabelled SE bars; Table 3 and Results give models adjusted for posttreatment variables and mediation/moderation results; main-text Results also explicitly give the no-controls usefulness multilevel coefficient, SE and p value. The five estimate records represent two output outcomes in one sample, with alternative statistical summaries of the same arm contrasts, and must not be treated as independent evidence. The study’s final sample is stated before the randomization step, supporting both randomized and analyzed totals; no postrandomization exclusions are reported. The extracted task is coded idea_generation because it solicits privacy-protection suggestions, although the broader intervention concerned ordinary workplace activity. No sample overlap with another paper is stated. No diversity outcome or documented AI-removal follow-up is reported. No statistics were calculated, no figure values were estimated, and no missing supplement values were inferred.
